questions.question: Classify milk and milk products. Explain their nutritive composition and / importance in growth and development.
questions.solution_html:
• Classify milk and milk products. Explain their nutritive composition and importance in
  • growth and development.
  • Classification of Milk and Milk Products ((4 marks))
  • A. Based on Fat Content / Standardization
  • • Whole milk: ~3.5–6% fat
  • • Toned milk: ~3% fat
  • • Double-toned milk: ~1.5% fat
  • • Skimmed milk: <0.5% fat
  • • Full-cream milk: ~6% fat
  • B. Based on Processing
  • • Pasteurized milk: Heated to destroy pathogens
  • • Sterilized milk: Longer shelf life, slight nutrient loss
  • • UHT milk: Long shelf life, minimal nutrient loss
  • • Homogenized milk: Uniform texture, no cream separation
  • • Reconstituted milk: Made from milk powder
  • • Concentrated products: Condensed milk, evaporated milk
  • C. Fermented Milk Products
  • • Curd, yoghurt, buttermilk, kefir
  • Nutritive Composition of Milk (per 100 ml) ((4 marks))
  • • Energy: 60–70 kcal
  • • Protein: ~3.2 g (high biological value)
  • • Fat: 3.5–4 g
  • • Carbohydrates: ~4.8 g (lactose)
  • • Minerals: Calcium (120 mg), phosphorus, potassium
  • • Vitamins: A, D, B2, B12
  • • Water: 85–88%
  • Importance in Growth and Development ((2 marks))
  • • Promotes bone and teeth formation (rich in calcium & phosphorus)
  • • Supports growth and tissue repair (high-quality protein)
  • • Important for children, adolescents, and pregnant women
  • • Helps in overall body development and maintenance
questions.final_answer: Option Based on Fat Content / Standardization
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
